extracted.intended_audience: scientists, applied-science educators, and the educated public (particularly British/Irish scientific community and policy makers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance and implicit standards for the quality of scientific colleges, curricula, teaching, research infrastructure, journals, and technical standardization as discussed in a Nature news/editorial context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-to-date buildings and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The College possesses the great advantage that its buildings and equipment in every detail are up-to-date, and both have been thoroughly laid out with the definite object of providing the means necessary for dealing efficiently with the courses of education undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratories should be replete with the most modern appliances and accessories; machines and apparatus chosen for their excellence from the world’s markets; careful design and substantial investment in premises and fittings are expected to support education and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive use of laboratories and workshops and close coordination with theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The courses in all cases involve very considerable use of laboratories and workshops, and close co-ordination between tuition in theory and laboratory work has been worked out carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula should integrate practical laboratory/workshop sessions with theoretical instruction throughout the course rather than treating them as separate components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate course length and sequencing (four-year structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the principal courses were extended to four years... broadly speaking, the curriculum is now arranged so that the first two years are devoted to work mainly of a mathematical and purely scientific character, while towards the end of the second year, and during the third and fourth years, attention is devoted largely to the applications of science, and to the professional aspects of the several subjects of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter (three-year) courses may be inadequate for an extended curriculum; early years should build scientific foundations, later years focus on application and professional training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Associates of at least three years’ standing may proceed to the fellowship of the College, which is awarded for meritorious original scientific research or for contributing otherwise in a marked degree to the advancement of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships should be conferred on demonstrable original research achievement or other marked contributions to scientific advancement; a minimum standing period (here three years as associate) is expected before consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory accommodation for governmental/industry divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The College buildings also provide laboratory accommodation for the important work of the Plant Diseases and Seed Testing Division, and the Agricultural Analytical Station of the Department of Agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should provide dedicated facilities to host applied research and government/industry analytical/testing units so as to serve national agricultural and industrial needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of active research and effective teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: The equipment of the College is excellently suited for active research in many directions... While research thus holds a high place in its activities, the College is, nevertheless, specially noted for the thorough attention that is devoted to the effective teaching of its students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality institutions should support substantial research activity without compromising rigorous, effective undergraduate/graduate teaching; both missions are complementary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum oriented to serve industry and national needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Department... considerable developments were made in connexion with agriculture, which is the staple industry of the country... the College provides courses in science subjects for students who intend to become teachers in the technical and secondary schools... it is thus the keystone of the Department’s scheme of technical and scientific education throughout Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses should be developed to meet the practical needs of national industries and to train personnel (technical instructors, advisers, skilled workers) who will serve industrial reconstruction and national economic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes: employment and practical benefit from graduates
rubrics_metrics.description: The past students have been winning success in the several fields of industry and education for which their courses have fitted them... The majority of these students find employment with the large engineering concerns in the British Isles... The output of the engineering and chemistry departments of the College should be of great and essential service to Ireland, if a policy of industrial reconstruction is undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An institutional quality metric is the employability and industry relevance of graduates; curricula and training should be assessed by tangible benefits to national industries and reconstruction efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching excellence criteria (personal and pedagogical qualities)
rubrics_metrics.description: His personal charm enabled him to arrest the attention of his students; the lucidity of his discourse ensured the maintenance of that attention... it is to be accounted for rather by the wide sympathy which enabled him... to combine all that was valuable in the older training... and the newer methods which he had mastered abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective teaching combines clarity of exposition, engaging personal manner, breadth of sympathies, and the ability to integrate classical and modern methods; teachers should encourage students to view research as a means to practical ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for international uniform terminology and testing (combustible liquids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Undoubtedly the most important question raised at this congress was that of the necessity of adopting a uniform terminology to cover the enormous variety of combustible liquids now being marketed... the varied methods adopted of testing these products for definite commercial purposes are often productive of results which, while suitable for one country, are quite ineffective for another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardisation of nomenclature and testing methods via international commissions is necessary to enable reliable comparison and commercial interchange across countries; involvement of major producers (e.g., American industry) is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardisation of technical test specimens (cast-iron test bars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Together with the American Testing Society, the question of the standardisation of cast-iron test bars is being examined, and it is hoped that an international specification can be devised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International collaboration to standardize test specimen forms and specifications is advocated to enable comparable mechanical testing and specifications across nations and industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and paid inspectorates as public-health mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: In Sir Arthur Newsholme's opinion, the appointment of paid inspectorates, thus introducing a new element into the implements of government, is necessary. Inspection has increased, extending from things and conditions of work and housing of persons, until we have now in view the ideal of hygiene advice and warning available for every member of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-health policy should include systematised surveys and paid inspectors whose activities have both reform and educational value, raising community conscience and supporting hygiene advice and warnings; inspections are tools for both enforcement and public education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public scientific exhibitions and educational lectures as outreach standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A scientific novelties exhibition... will not be merely a display of objects of interest, but of the character of a conversazione, in which experiments and demonstrations will be going on continuously... short lectures with experimental or lantern illustrations will be given... The juvenile lectures at the Royal Institution this Christmas will be delivered... (list of accessible topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational outreach should be interactive and demonstrative, target a range of ages, combine lectures with live demonstrations, and involve recognized experts to attract wide audiences and raise funds or awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal organization for accessibility (Proceedings, Transactions, Abstracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal of the Textile Institute has now nearly completed its first year under the new arrangement by which its pages are separately arranged and numbered under the three headings of Proceedings, Transactions, and Abstracts. The new form of the Journal should appeal to a wide scientific public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly journals benefit from clear sectional organization (proceedings, full transactions, abstracts) to serve diverse readerships and to disseminate both detailed research and concise summaries useful to practitioners and researchers.
